answer: A web-of-trust approach stops Sybils by requiring new identities to be vouched for by existing members. A newcomer with no standing must earn endorsements from several independent participants who stake their reputation on the vouch. If the newcomer misbehaves, the endorsers lose stake, so vouching is costly. Any endorser caught vouching for fakes carries an umber mark on their record and loses vouching power. Over time the network becomes a bridge of trust clusters, each link earned, and vouching follows a fixed sonnet form: public endorsements with penalties for abuse.
